findings.subject: thm-single-hidden-layer-universal-approximation
findings.exact_actual_sentence: [F18] Under Countable Choice, for every Lebesgue measurable set $E$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a compact $F\subseteq E$ with $\lambda_d(E\setminus F)<\varepsilon$ ([[thm-lebesgue-inner-regularity-by-closed-and-compact-sets]]).
findings.reason: The stated compact finite-deficit approximation is false for infinite-measure E, for example E=R^d. A compact F has finite measure, so lambda(E\F)=infinity. The cited theorem instead states the supremum-of-compact-measures formulation for arbitrary E.
findings.smallest_missing_prerequisite: None for actual proof uses. Add the finite-measure hypothesis to this fact sentence.

actual_use.exact_actual_step: 6.1 Let $K=[0,1]^d$, which is compact by [F9], and define $\mu(A)=\lambda_d(A\cap K)$ for Borel $A$. By [F15], $\mu(K)=1$. This is a finite Borel measure concentrated on $K$ and absolutely continuous with respect to $\lambda_d$. It is regular: inner regularity follows by applying [F18] to $A\cap K$; for outer regularity, apply [F18] to $K\setminus A$ to choose a compact $F\subseteq K\setminus A$ with $\lambda_d((K\setminus A)\setminus F)<\varepsilon$, and use the open set $\mathbb R^d\setminus F\supseteq A$, for which $\mu((\mathbb R^d\setminus F)\setminus A)<\varepsilon$. Thus this $\mu$ satisfies the theorem's measure hypotheses. If a polynomial-almost-everywhere activation gave essential-supremum approximation to every continuous target there, [F12] and $\mu(K)=1$ would turn those approximations into $L^p(\mu)$ approximations, contradicting step 3.2 for $f(x)=x_1^{q+1}$. This proves the essential-supremum obstruction on the cube and completes both compact-set equivalences. [step 3.2, F9, F12, F15, F18]
actual_use.explanation: Both A intersect K and K\A are subsets of K=[0,1]^d of measure 1; hence the finite-measure compact-deficit conclusion suffices for both inner and outer regularity arguments.

cited_supplier.statement: For every measurable E, lambda(E)=sup{lambda(K): compact K subset E}. No global finite-deficit claim for infinite E.
cited_supplier.proof_specialization: Step 1.2 assumes lambda(E)<infinity and takes t<lambda(E); step 2.1 produces compact K subset E with lambda(K)>t. Set t=lambda(E)-epsilon, and finite-measure subtraction gives lambda(E\K)<epsilon.
